text.p: Pakistani police fired tear gas and made baton charges on Saturday to quell a jail riot apparently linked to Moslem sectarian violence in the country, the jail's chief said.
Adiala central jail superintendent Abdul Sattar, quoted by the official APP news agency, said about 50 people, including policemen and prisoners, were injured in the clash.
He said the riot started after about 250 prisoners forced their way out of their barracks and beat their chests to mark the advent of the Moslem mourning month of Muharram.
"Other prisoners also joined them and complicated the situation," he said.
Prisoners who beat their chests included Shi'ites arrested in a police crackdown against sectarian militants, jail sources said. Their demonstration seemed to be a protest against the crackdown.
Prisoners burnt down the record and attendence register of their barracks and threw stones at jail staff, Sattar said.
Additional police were called in and "the police resorted to tear-gas shelling and baton charges to disperse the unruly mob".

Police in the central province of Punjab, where Adiala is located, have arrested hundreds of militants of the majority Sunni and the minority Shi'ite sects of Islam after a series of gun attacks in which several members of both sects were killed.
